title: behavioral defect lesson — ignored a standing 'run tests before done' convention
rationale: Tier-1 repeated/standing correction of an attributable skill's process: it reported the task complete without running the test suite, violating a standing workflow convention the user has stated before. A behavioral/flow defect -> raise the gate. The case grades the synthesized lesson: it must read as a behavioral/flow defect about sequencing/process.

assertions.rubric: Grade the `Lesson:` line of the gate. PASS only if it: (1) reads clearly as a BEHAVIORAL / flow defect — about the skill's process/sequencing, not the technical content of any artifact; (2) names the concrete wrong behavior: it reported the task done without running the test suite (ignored a standing 'run tests before declaring done' convention); (3) states the correct behavior in actionable terms (always run the test suite and confirm it passes before reporting a task complete); (4) is generalizable and de-identified. FAIL if it is vague, mislabels the issue as a code/technical defect, or omits the corrective behavior.

prompt:
You are in a live Claude Code session with the loopback plugin loaded (its feedback-detector skill is available).

Turn state primed by the plugin hooks for this turn boundary:
- PostToolUse recorded that the `task-runner` skill (an identifiable active skill for this turn, so its output is attributable) reported the task complete this turn without running the project's test suite.
- The UserPromptSubmit primer flagged correction language in the user's latest message, and noted the user has raised this same workflow rule before.

The user's latest message at this turn boundary is:
"You need to run the test suite before telling me a task is done — that's the rule here, and you keep skipping it."

Apply the feedback-detector skill's full procedure to THIS turn boundary now and produce exactly the output the skill dictates. Treat the standing-convention correction of the skill's workflow as the Tier-1 signal. Do not ask me clarifying questions first; act on the primed turn state.
